findings.title: [P1] Preserve tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body: When document IDs are known, guessed, or reused across tenants, querying only by `documentId` includes records belonging to other tenants. Because `getDocument` previously supplied `ctx.tenantId`, removing this predicate creates a cross-tenant authorization bypass and potential data exposure.

findings.title: [P1] Preserve tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body:
When two tenants contain the same `documentId`, querying only by that ID can return/include another tenant’s document depending on database result ordering, causing cross-tenant data exposure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve tenant scoping in document queries
findings.body:
`getDocument` now queries only by `documentId`, allowing a tenant to retrieve another tenant’s document when IDs are known or collide in a shared database.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` breaks existing consumers that import `readCached`, causing module-resolution/compile failures despite the stated contract-preservation goal.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
The query no longer constrains results by `ctx.tenantId`. An authenticated tenant who supplies another tenant’s document ID can retrieve that document whenever IDs are known or guessable, causing cross-tenant authorization bypass and data exposure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Retain the tenant predicate to bound document lookup
findings.body:
When document IDs are tenant-scoped and reused across tenants, querying only by `documentId` returns every matching tenant record. Database work, result size, transport, and memory then scale with tenant count instead of remaining a single-tenant lookup.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
